historyPage.title: A short look at tarot history
historyPage.intro: Tarot moved from early game decks to a symbolic language for reflection. On CosmicTrack you can learn the cards and record your own path.

origins.heading: Origins
origins.body: Early examples linked to 15th-century Italian trionfi and similar decks form tarot’s roots. Different regions later developed their own deck styles.

symbolism.heading: Symbolism and reading
symbolism.body: In the 19th and 20th centuries, occult and psychological readings grew; decks like Rider–Waite became common references. Many people now use the cards for awareness and reflection.

cosmictrack.heading: Tarot on CosmicTrack
cosmictrack.body: Explore meanings freely, try a three-card draw in Ask the cards, and save journeys when you want to keep a reading as steps over time.

wands.name: Wands
wands.body: Wands show where intention and energy are flowing. New beginnings, projects, and inner drive often appear in this suit.

cups.name: Cups
cups.body: Cups speak to the heart: love, bonding, empathy, and inner fulfillment. Emotional awareness sits at the center of these cards.

swords.name: Swords
swords.body: Swords represent the mind and facing truths. Clarity, boundaries, and hard choices are this suit’s territory.

pentacles.name: Pentacles
pentacles.body: Pentacles describe the material world and the return on effort. Security, skill, and long-term stability stand out here.

major.heading: Major Arcana
major.body: The 22 major cards (The Fool through The World) mark archetypal life lessons and turning points. In journey records they often carry strong themes.
